Dr. Todd A. Lefkowitz is a board-certified ophthalmologist who works as an expert ophthalmology witness for attorneys handling eye-care cases in Ohio. He has already reviewed cases from Ohio and has testified at trial there, and he takes on work for mainly plaintiff and sometimes defense counsel.

Attorneys who need an expert ophthalmologist witness in Ohio can work with Dr. Lefkowitz remotely for most of a case. Records review, calls and depositions are handled by phone or video conference, for cases in Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati or a smaller county court.

Ophthalmologist Expert Witness Services in Ohio

Dr. Lefkowitz can support an Ohio case from the first look at the records through trial:

  • Review of medical records and a clear opinion on whether the standard of care was met
  • Review of the records ahead of an Ohio affidavit of merit
  • Affidavits in support of your case if merited
  • Deposition testimony, in person or by video conference
  • Trial testimony, with travel to Ohio when needed

Dr. Lefkowitz understands that some cases are time sensitive. Once the case is received, he can offer a quick turnaround.

Ohio Rules That Shape an Eye Malpractice Case

Ohio requires one or more affidavits of merit to be filed with a medical claim complaint for each defendant where expert testimony is needed (Ohio Civil Rule 10(D)(2)). The court can extend the time to file by up to 90 days for good cause.

The filing deadline is one year from when the claim accrues (Ohio Rev. Code § 2305.113). If written notice is sent before that year ends, the case can be filed within 180 days after the notice. In most cases no claim can be filed more than four years after the act or omission. Sending the case for an expert ophthalmology witness review early gives your team time to act on the opinion.

This is general information for attorneys, not legal advice. Your counsel should confirm how these rules apply to your case.

Dr. Lefkowitz is an independent and ethical expert. You can see every state where he has reviewed cases on his expert ophthalmologist witness services page.

How to Start Your Ohio Case

  1. Email talefkowitzmd@gmail.com or fill in the form on the Contact Me page. Add a short summary of the case, the court and any deadline.
  2. Dr. Lefkowitz replies to talk through the case and confirm it fits his expertise.
  3. Send Dr. Lefkowitz the medical records. He will review them and provide an expert ophthalmology witness report with his opinion.

Please contact Dr. Lefkowitz only if you are an attorney or are working with legal representation.

Ohio Expert Ophthalmology Witness FAQs

Q

Does Dr. Lefkowitz work for both plaintiff and defense in Ohio?

Dr. Lefkowitz reviews Ohio eye cases for mainly plaintiff and sometimes defense counsel, but provides the same independent opinion either way.

Q

Can Dr. Lefkowitz provide an Ohio affidavit of merit?

He can review the records and discuss whether his opinion supports the claim. Under Ohio Civil Rule 10(D)(2) the affidavit of merit is filed with the complaint and must come from an expert who meets Ohio's requirements.

Q

Does he need to travel to Ohio?

Not for most of the work. Case review and depositions can be done by phone or video conference. He will travel to Ohio for trial testimony.

Q

How soon should an Ohio case be sent for review?

As early as possible. Ohio generally allows one year from when the claim accrues, or 180 days after a timely notice letter (Ohio Rev. Code § 2305.113). Your counsel should confirm the deadline for your case.
